findingReviews.rationale: This is a serialized public author response. The command term appears in quoted capability discussion and is not executable source.
This is a serialized review response describing a third-party source finding, not a manager runtime entry point or executed command.
This line defines a literal module-name detector for fixed-source review. It recognizes child_process imports as a signal and does not invoke child_process.
The manager invokes the official DSH CLI through execFile with fixed argv and shell disabled. This explicit command capability is already disclosed in the high-risk Catalog entry.
Guardian launches the resolved DSH executable through execFile with bounded arguments and no shell interpolation. The optional supervisor capability remains disclosed.
The upgrader calls a pinned executable using a fixed argument array through execFile. It does not build a shell command; restricted command use remains disclosed.
Guardian uses fixed execFile arguments to start and inspect the DSH process. This is the separately planned optional supervisor, not hidden install-time code.
Legacy repair calls the official CLI with fixed argv rather than shell text. Its file writes and command use are covered by the manager plan and backup flow.
This is a regular expression describing risky patterns in candidate plugin text. It is review logic and does not perform a child-process operation.
The critical match is the scanner own inert regex literal for mining indicators. It is not mining behavior; the exact scanner file hash is bound to this review.

permissionReview.reason: Store 0.9.22 restores a searchable Catalog and Desktop browsing/detail/lifecycle UI. Desktop adaptation is a label, while DSH Desktop official pluginManager checks DSH compatibility for approved entries. Catalog-blocked entries such as build-dsh-plugin remain visible but cannot be installed from the Store under current admission policy. Real Desktop Profile acceptance is still unverified; preserve the existing web-only Catalog claim.

toolViewReview.rationale: Scanner hits are in admission-review and author-reply JSON records. They are neither runtime entry files nor declared Cordis Tool-view components; no protected DSH component ownership change is present.
